FACT A:
entity: India textile export basket
attribute: Apparel export share percentage
value: 42 per cent one
normalised value: 42.0 percent
period: 2023 (2023-01-01 to 2023-12-31)
estimate type: actual
measurement basis: not stated
attributed to: the document itself
document: 01-india-economic-survey-2024-25-excerpt.pdf; publisher: Government of India; published: 2024-07-01
page label: 94
evidence verified: True (normalized)
quote: "with apparel constituting 42 per cent of the export basket (USD 14.6 billion)"

FACT B:
entity: India
attribute: global market share of apparel exports
value: 2.6 per cent
normalised value: 2.6 percent
period: 2023 (2023-01-01 to 2023-12-31)
estimate type: unknown
measurement basis: not stated
attributed to: World Intellectual Property Organisation
document: 02-rbi-annual-report-2024-25-excerpt.pdf; publisher: Reserve Bank of India; published: unknown
page label: 25
evidence verified: True (normalized)
quote: "rose from 2.1 per cent in 2000 to 2.6 per cent in 2023 (World Intellectual Property Organisation, 2024)"

Rule-engine hypothesis: attributed figure differs from first-party

Decide the verdict.

request.system:
You compare two facts extracted from two documents and decide how they relate.

Verdicts:
- corroborates: same quantity, same period, same basis, compatible values (allow rounding).
- superseded: same quantity and period, but a later data vintage or a revision replaces the
  earlier value; name which fact is newer.
- context_explained: the values differ because the period, scope/basis, unit or attribution
  differs; name that dimension. This is not a contradiction.
- contradicts: same quantity, period, basis and unit carry incompatible values.
- unresolved: the evidence does not settle it; give your best hypothesis in the explanation.

Use only the fields and quotes provided. Keep the explanation under 60 words and cite the
distinguishing phrase from each quote.

response.explanation: Fact A refers to apparel's share of India's total textile export basket ("apparel constituting 42 per cent of the export basket"), whereas Fact B refers to India's global market share of apparel exports ("global market share of apparel exports... rose... to 2.6 per cent"). The two facts measure entirely different metrics.
